question_name: Is boot_android's per-boot repair stock Rockchip behavior or a TXCZ patch?
findings: The `boot_android` U-Boot command (do_boot_android, in cmd/boot_android.c) and the flow it drives (android_bootloader_boot_flow, in common/android_bootloader.c) are NOT Rockchip inventions. android_bootloader.c carries a 'Copyright (C) 2016 The Android Open Source Project' / SPDX BSD-2-Clause header and originated as an upstream U-Boot mailing-list patch series, 'Initial support for the Android Bootloader flow' (lists.denx.de, U-Boot list, April 2017), which added cmd 'boot_android' plus BCB (bootloader control block) parsing, A/B slot selection, and Android image loading to mainline U-Boot around the v2017.09 era. Rockchip's rockchip-linux/u-boot fork (and downstream forks such as rockchip-toybrick/u-boot) carried this code forward essentially unmodified in its control flow, adding only Rockchip/RK-specific hooks: rk_avb_get_current_slot() and other rk_avb_* calls that wire in Rockchip's own Android Verified Boot (AVB) integration for cryptographic signature/rollback-index checking. Reading the actual do_boot_android and android_bootloader_boot_flow logic (confirmed via direct file retrieval from rockchip-linux/u-boot's release branch and rockchip-toybrick/u-boot) shows the function: (1) reads the BCB from the misc partition, (2) picks a slot / decides normal vs recovery vs fastboot, (3) loads the boot or recovery image, (4) if AVB is enabled, cryptographically verifies the loaded image and on failure resets/tries another slot, (5) assembles the kernel cmdline and calls android_bootloader_boot_kernel -> bootm. At no point does stock upstream or stock Rockchop code write, restore, or repopulate an arbitrary partition (system, boot, recovery, etc.) from a reference/golden copy as part of this flow -- AVB failure triggers a reset/retry-slot, not a partition rewrite, and there is no A/B non-A/B 'restore' path in this code at all. Given this device is explicitly non-A/B (rk3326_sgo, per device_facts) and per the outline's own prior finding that this device's uboot.bin carries a distinct '#txcz' build tag confirming a vendor-modified U-Boot fork, the observed whole-partition-repopulation-from-reference behavior (surviving into both Recovery and normal Android, before init.rc, with a fresh inode each time) cannot be explained by any documented stock Rockchip/AOSP boot_android or android_bootloader code path. It would necessarily be a bespoke addition: either a TXCZ patch injected directly into the compiled boot_android/android_bootloader binary (replacing or wrapping the stock AVB-failure/reset behavior with an actual partition-restore-from-reference step), or a separate custom command/board-init hook spliced into the U-Boot boot sequence ahead of or alongside boot_android (e.g. in board.c / a custom preboot hook), since bootcmd on this device is 'boot_android ${devtype} ${devnum};boot_fit;bootrkp;run distro_bootcmd' and nothing in the public upstream chain performs partition restoration. On the version-dating question: 'U-Boot 2017.09' is a real, well-documented, findable line -- both real upstream U-Boot (mainline v2017.09, released Sept 2017) and Rockchip's own release-20171218 tag on rockchip-linux/u-boot explicitly state they are based on mainline v2017.09 (per that repo's public Releases page). So the base version string is genuine and datable to roughly late 2017 through the point Rockchip rebased to a newer mainline version. However, the exact short git-describe hash 'g2807ac1' quoted for this device's build does not appear in any public commit of rockchip-linux/u-boot or any other Rockchip u-boot fork found via GitHub commit search (a coincidence-style search for that hash prefix returned only unrelated repositories, none of which are U-Boot trees). This is consistent with -- though not proof of -- 'g2807ac1' being a commit from TXCZ's own private/downstream fork built on top of a public Rockchip 2017.09-based tree, rather than a commit that exists in any tree currently published on GitHub.
relevance_to_our_symptoms: This fully explains WHY the repair mechanism was invisible to plaintext string search inside the compiled boot_android command (as already suspected in outline.yaml): boot_android is real compiled C code, and the stock/upstream version of that C code (confirmed here directly from source) has no restore-from-reference logic to find in the first place -- there is nothing 'stock' to grep for, because stock boot_android's only partition-protective behavior is AVB signature verification-and-reset, not content-restoration. This finding rules out the hypothesis that the observed behavior is a known, documented, upstream Rockchip/AOSP feature that we're simply failing to recognize; it must be OEM-injected code, most likely patched directly into the compiled do_boot_android/android_bootloader_boot_flow binary (or a preboot hook that runs before it), since the outline already established the bootcmd variable runs boot_android before anything else, and the symptom (fresh inode, wipes both Recovery and normal-boot targets, occurs before init.rc parses) is exactly the kind of pre-Android-userspace, pre-kernel-mount behavior only U-Boot itself (or a stage before it) could produce. It does not, by itself, pinpoint the exact injected code or confirm whether the restore source is embedded in uboot.bin, trust.bin, or elsewhere -- that remains for the static-analysis/disassembly and compressed-reference-image research items. It also does not explain why a non-A/B device would have any AVB-style rk_avb_* code paths at all (worth flagging as a related but separate question for follow-up), since rk_avb_get_current_slot() as seen in the reference source assumes A/B; on a non-A/B build this code is likely compiled out or stubbed, which further supports that whatever restore logic exists here is custom rather than a normal-Rockchip-AVB byproduct.
confidence: high -- based on directly reading the actual upstream U-Boot mailing-list patch, the actual rockchip-linux/u-boot released source (release branch, and independently rockchip-toybrick/u-boot's common/android_bootloader.c), and Rockchip's own public release notes; the one lower-confidence sub-claim is that 'g2807ac1' is unfindable in public trees, which is a negative result from GitHub's commit search (not exhaustive/cryptographically definitive) rather than a proof of non-existence.
sources_or_method: WebSearch + WebFetch against: (1) github.com/rockchip-linux/u-boot (repo home, branches list, Releases page, cmd/boot_android.c and arch/arm/mach-rockchip/ on the 'release' branch); (2) github.com/rockchip-toybrick/u-boot common/android_bootloader.c (full file content fetched and read for copyright header and control flow); (3) lists.denx.de U-Boot mailing list archive thread 'Initial support for the Android Bootloader flow' (April 2017) and the companion lore.kernel.org thread 'cmd: Add boot_android command'; (4) github.com/search commit search for the hash prefix '2807ac1' across all public repos, returned via WebFetch (no U-Boot repository match found). All quoted file contents were fetched live from GitHub raw/blob URLs in this session, not recalled from training data, precisely because this device's exact TXCZ fork is not itself public and only the upstream/Rockchip lineage could be checked.
safe_next_step: Cross-reference this finding against the locally pulled uboot.bin using the already-planned static-disassembly research item: now that we know exactly what STOCK do_boot_android/android_bootloader_boot_flow should look like (BCB read -> slot/mode decision -> image load -> optional AVB check -> bootm, with AVB failure causing a reset/slot-retry and no partition writes), a disassembler pass can specifically diff the local binary's do_boot_android code shape against that expected stock shape and flag any extra basic blocks that reference ext4write/mmc-write-style calls or a fixed reference-partition offset -- i.e. use this provenance result as the 'known good' baseline to make the binary diff/trace targeted rather than open-ended. Also worth a follow-up WebSearch specifically for 'rockchip-linux/u-boot rk3326_sgo' or 'TXCZ uboot rk3326' board configs/defconfigs to see if any TXCZ or rk3326_sgo board files ever leaked to a public fork (some vendor SDKs get partially open-sourced by hobbyists), which could locate the exact downstream tree g2807ac1 belongs to.
risky_next_step_if_pursued: If the safe static/documentary analysis above is inconclusive, the only way to get fully authoritative confirmation of what code the on-device boot_android actually runs would be to extract live diagnostic output from the device itself -- e.g. interrupting U-Boot at the serial/UART console (if one is exposed) to run 'md' or 'bdinfo'-style commands, or dumping boot log verbosity to see if any restore step prints a message -- or reflashing a modified U-Boot (with the restore logic patched out or with debug printfs added) via Maskrom/fastboot to observe behavior directly. This would require physical device access, serial/UART wiring or Maskrom-mode flashing, and carries real risk of corrupting the uboot/trust partitions and bricking the device if the write is interrupted, malformed, or targets the wrong offset -- especially since this device's exact U-Boot build (g2807ac1) is not the public Rockchip release, so the safe stock U-Boot binaries available for this platform are not guaranteed to be byte-compatible replacements.
risk_level: high -- brick risk, recovery would depend on Maskrom-mode access to the SoC, which per the user's existing HY300 device findings is understood to require hardware-level access this project has treated as the real practical blocker; this device-touching step should not be taken unless the safe static-analysis paths are exhausted first.
